column1: # CAPTURE-BASIS GUARD (added 2026-08-28 by HENRY, answering WALTER SIG-W-20260828-013's second ASK clause: "consider whether the ledger's capture-time policy needs a guard, since its own note asserted the property the value lacked").

# WHAT FAILED: the 2026-08-26 row's Source note read "SETTLED CLOSES ONLY" -- a BLANKET policy assertion -- while its Brent cell held a live intraday tick from the NEXT trade date on the WRONG contract. The note asserted a property the value lacked, and the note is what stopped a reader from checking. A POLICY STATED IN PROSE CANNOT ENFORCE ITSELF, and a row-level claim cannot vouch for cells of mixed provenance.
# THE GUARD -- three rules, each checkable by eye at the cell rather than by trusting the row note:

#   G1 BASIS-AT-THE-CELL. A blanket basis claim in Source ("SETTLED CLOSES ONLY") binds ONLY the cells it can vouch for. Any cell whose basis differs MUST carry its basis inline next to the value or be n/a. Never let the row note be the sole carrier of a basis claim.

#   G2 FOREIGN VALUES NAME SOURCE + INSTRUMENT. A cell taken from another desk's published figure names the SOURCE and the CONTRACT/SERIES (e.g. "BZV26 Oct-26"), never the desk alone. A continuous-front ticker is not an instrument identity -- it can roll between its own daily and intraday series (SIG-W-20260828-012), so "BZ=F" alone does not identify what was measured.

#   G3 DISAGREEMENT IS ROUTED, NOT JUST RECORDED. If own-instrument and a publisher of record disagree, record BOTH with both bases AND route the disagreement back to the publisher THE SAME SESSION. Recording it and deferring silently is what turned a caught error into a propagated one on 8/26. [[finding_owner_of_record_means_authoritative_not_correct]]

# POSITIVE CONTROL, do not 'fix' it: the 2026-08-21 row's Brent/Gas n/a with "Brent NOT pulled -- do not infer" is the guard working. An honest n/a beats a plausible number. PROME concurred 2026-08-28.

ONE-CELL FIX -- SPX 7675.70 / VIX 15.21 / HY 267 / CCC 1031 on this row are all CORRECT and were NOT touched. ** WHAT THIS ROW IS THE RECORD OF, stated because -015 inverts the blame and I am not taking the flattering half on trust either: I DID run the check, my own bar DID disagree, I DID write the disagreement down, and I deferred to the publisher of record anyway -- and the wrong number won BECAUSE of where it came from. [[finding_owner_of_record_means_authoritative_not_correct]]. The remedy is NOT a stronger disclaimer: the disclaimer was present, the 8/20 precedent was cited BY NAME, the discrepancy was MEASURED, and the deference was explicit and reasoned. THE RULE I AM TAKING FORWARD: when my own instrument disagrees with a publisher of record, the cell carries BOTH figures with both bases named, and the disagreement is ROUTED BACK TO THE PUBLISHER THE SAME SESSION -- deferring silently is what turned a caught error into a propagated one. ** PROVENANCE + FRAMING, added same session on PROME's routing: the reconciled figure is BRENT's (commit 37955e32f), WALTER concurred, DOCKET-certified 2026-08-28. PROME's framing, adopted: record this as AUTHORITY-OF-RECORD CORRECTED UPSTREAM, not as a caveat failure -- the check ran, it FIRED, the disagreement was written down, and the wrong number won on authority. AND THE 8/21 n/a IS GOOD DISCIPLINE, NOT PART OF THE DEFECT: that row refuses to record a Brent value it did not pull ('Brent NOT pulled -- do not infer') and that refusal is exactly right; do not 'fill it in' on a later pass.
